t.E171.agn: In May 2021 EFSA concluded that titanium dioxide can no longer be considered safe as a food additive because a concern for genotoxicity (damage to genetic material) could not be ruled out. In the EU its use in food has been banned since 7 August 2022 (Regulation 2022/63). In Türkiye it was removed from the list by a regulation dated 13 October 2023; foods containing it were allowed to be placed on the market until 1 April 2024.
t.E171.body: Titanium dioxide is very poorly absorbed when taken orally (in mice most likely less than 0.5%). Absorbed particles are eliminated from the body very slowly (half-life estimated at 200–450 days); they may therefore accumulate in the body.
t.E171.eff.0.t: Not considered safe in food because a concern for damage to genetic material (genotoxicity) could not be ruled out; it cannot be used in food in the EU since 2022 and in Türkiye since 2024
t.E171.eval: In 2021 EFSA could not rule out the genotoxicity concern; its use in food was banned in the EU in 2022. In Türkiye, under the Food Additives Regulation dated 13 October 2023, foods containing E171 were allowed to be placed on the market until 1 April 2024.
t.E171.prod: Pure titanium dioxide produced from titanium ore by chemical processes.
t.E171.summary: A white mineral pigment. It was used to give an opaque white colour to confectionery coatings, chewing gum and white sauces.
t.E171.what: It gave food an opaque white colour.
t.agency.EU_banned_2022: Authorisation as a food additive withdrawn in the EU.
t.agency.TR_withdrawn_2024: In Türkiye, removed from the authorised list.
